view.name: Document viewer with visualizer
view.description: Lecture PDF with inline concept tag pills on the left and the Visualizer pane on the right showing a generated graph for the selected concept.

regions.label: App top bar: Upload, Library, open document tab with MANUAL badge; Synced status, 7/7 viz ready, settings and account icons
PDF lecture notes rendered as page canvases, with coloured inline concept chips, a hover tooltip and a floating page pager plus zoom
Visualizer panel: mode dropdown menu, Graph type chip and title, line chart of carrier saturation vs diffusion, overflow menu and a caption footer

evidence.note: Persistent top bar with global links, a document tab, status and account controls

patterns.rationale: Only one document tab is open, next to Upload/Library links styled like tabs. I couldn't confirm whether several documents can be open as peer tabs.

evidence.note: Raised active document tab joined to the content area
Amber label pill on the document tab
Fixed-layout PDF page rendered to canvas, with a 'page 1' footer
Floating page pager and zoom controls (100%, +, −)
Previous/next page buttons around a jump-to-page indicator
Hover label under the active concept chip shows the full type and title
Document pane and visualizer pane sit side by side. Clicking a chip in the document changes what the right pane shows. Hovering the divider did not reveal a resize handle.
Two-series line chart (purple GLUT carrier, grey simple diffusion) with axis titles 'uptake rate' and '[glucose] (mM)', a legend and gridlines

Dropdown (checked live) lists Visualizer, Knowledge Graph, Chat, Flashcards, Quizzes and Feynman, each with an icon and a description. The ⋯ overflow menu offers Regenerate visualization and Download work context.

patterns.rationale: The inline chips act as item views for 7 generated visualizations. Each chip is colour-coded by type and has a truncated title, and it opens its detail in the right pane. They are spread through the document text rather than gathered into a collection overview, so this may not count.

evidence.note: Active chip whose detail (the graph) shows in the right pane
Formula chip. Clicking it (checked live) swaps the right pane to a formula derivation.

patterns.rationale: Concept chips are anchored to text spans in the PDF and open content in a side panel. However, they are system-generated tags for visualizations, not discussion or feedback between people, so the collaborate framing may not apply.

evidence.note: 3D Model chip anchored after the phrase 'phospholipid bilayer'
Visualizations appear to be generated ('Regenerate visualization' in the overflow menu), but nothing explicitly marks them as AI-made or cites sources

structure.layout: Desktop app shell: thin top bar with Upload/Library links and an open-document tab, then a fixed two-pane split. The PDF reader is on the left (page canvas, floating pager and zoom). A visualizer panel is on the right (mode dropdown, type chip and title header, chart canvas, caption footer).

aesthetics.typography: GeistSans throughout the UI: tabs, buttons, chips, tooltip, panel header and caption. The PDF content uses the document's own sans font with bold headings.
aesthetics.typeScale: UI chrome is small and quiet: 13px/500 for tabs, 12px/500 for controls, 14px for the panel title, 10–11px/600 for chips, badges and tooltip. Hierarchy comes from the document itself: a ~28px bold H1, ~20px bold H2s and ~13px body text.

notes: Distinctive device: small pastel pill chips (rounded 999px, 1px tinted border, light shadow) sit inline on the PDF text at the concept they explain. They are colour-coded by visualization type: rose = 3D Model, lavender = Formula, blue = Graph, mint = Source, amber = Animation. Each has a line icon and a truncated title. The active chip gets a dark outline ring plus a tooltip, and the right panel's header repeats the type chip (e.g. a blue 'Graph' pill) and the title. The right panel switches between tools (Visualizer, Knowledge Graph, Chat, Flashcards, Quizzes, Feynman) via a dropdown menu with descriptions. The Formula view shows a 'HEADLINE' KaTeX equation card and numbered step-by-step derivation cards. The UI uses a warm off-white (#f6f5f2) canvas around white rounded panels (12px), and the pager and zoom controls float as small white pills at the bottom of the document pane. In the full-page capture, the chips are mispositioned at the panel's left edge because the panel was stretched for the capture.
